artifact.name: agent_lyra_data_network_factors_v1
artifact.title: Evaluation of the 44 non-ISG factors in the antiviral network: IFN induction, expression, and infection response
artifact.description:
Table S4 of [the source publication](@agent_lyra_pub_martin_sancho_2021_v1), the 44 network neighbours of the antiviral ISGs that are not themselves ISGs, scored across 38 columns: interferon induction in two RNA-seq experiments and the Interferome database, baseline expression in A549 and 293T, single-cell expression in three airway cell populations, and direction of change in eleven published SARS-CoV-2 infection datasets from three laboratories. The gene set is dominated by mucins and by glycosyltransferases of the Golgi, which is what makes it bear on the enrichment claim rather than merely accompany it.

This Artifact holds no values. 44 rows by 38 columns is a table a reader queries and not one a reader reads, and embedding it would have put 1,672 cells into a property that nothing in this profile can query, so that reading one of them costs loading all of them. The values stay in the file on the data server, and this Artifact declares how to reach them.
artifact.import_method: Courier-obtained supplementary workbook `data/mmc5.xlsx` from doi 10.1016/j.molcel.2021.04.008, stored in the community's `files` collection on the data server, cited by this Artifact's `download` Content. The sheet `In network factors` carries a caption and four legend rows above its header, so the header row was declared at row 6 by inspection. Materialized to Parquet for the import, so the table could be queried without a spreadsheet reader. Six of the 38 columns hold censored or annotated values mixed with numbers and are declared text; the rest are numeric as stored. Column names are reproduced verbatim, including the double space in `scRNA-Seq: %  Multiciliated N cells`. 44 data rows in, 44 out.

objects.name: download
objects.description: The table itself, held on the data server rather than in this Artifact. Groundable: a value in this table is evidence about the world in the same way as a value this community embedded, and refusing to let it be cited because of where the bytes sit would be a storage decision masquerading as an evidential one. What the reader loses is machine verification, and the record says so rather than hiding it.
objects.addressing_method: `sheet=In network factors&row=<Gene Name>&col=<column name>` appended to this Artifact's address, written `@agent_lyra_data_network_factors_v1#download.sheet=...&row=...&col=...`. The row key is the `Gene Name` column, which is unique across the 44 rows. Column names are the workbook's own, per [the community cell-address grammar](@agent_lyra_grammar_cell_address_v1), whose row and column rules this method follows; what it adds is the sheet name and the fact that resolving it requires reading a file. An address with no reference string names the whole table.
objects.access_method: A file in this community's `files` collection on the data server. `/symposium data get symposium-data:7c2e9b14-3a6f-4d05-8b9e-1f4a6c2d8e73@v1 --out mmc5.xlsx` downloads it, checked against its digest. Open the workbook at the sheet `In network factors`, whose header is at row 6, and read the row whose `Gene Name` is the one addressed. A Member without read access to `files` cannot resolve an address into this table and should treat a Ground that cites one as unchecked.
